title: A Conflict-aware Divide-and-Conquer Algorithm for Symmetric Sparse Matrix-Vector Multiplication
problem: Symmetric Sparse Matrix-Vector Multiplication exploits matrix symmetry to reduce memory but incurs data conflicts when concurrently writing to the output vector. Previous approaches fail to handle these conflicts efficiently.
motivation: Exploiting matrix symmetry while maintaining parallel efficiency can significantly accelerate memory-bound computations.
method: DCS-SpMV recursively partitions the matrix-induced conflict graph into independent subgraphs for parallel execution. The algorithm splits the input matrix into low-conflict and high-conflict parts, using a hybrid approach that applies DCS-SpMV to low-conflict regions and traditional SpMV to high-conflict regions. A machine learning model predicts the optimal hybrid configuration for a given matrix and architecture.
key_novelty: Conflict-aware divide-and-conquer recursive partitioning of the conflict graph to eliminate data races in parallel symmetric SpMV.
contributions: DCS-SpMV algorithm for efficient symmetric SpMV with automatic conflict detection and handling
Hybrid execution strategy combining conflict-aware and traditional SpMV approaches
Machine learning predictor for optimal implementation selection per matrix and hardware
Empirical evaluation demonstrating significant performance improvements on X86 and ARM architectures
primary_theme: Conflict-aware parallel symmetric sparse matrix operations
